title: Meta Q3 Earnings: AI spending, revenue beat & new stock class - ​Meta beats Q3 estimates as AI spending surges | The Economic Times
text:
Meta Platforms reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter revenue, driven by advertising growth, while raising its investment ambitions in artificial intelligence. The results spotlight whether its core business can sustain the rising cost of its AI expansion. (Sources: Yahoo Finance, Reuters, The Wall Street Journal)

Revenue rose to $64.6 billion in the September quarter from $51.2 billion a year earlier. Advertising revenue climbed to about $63.1 billion, highlighting the continued strength of Meta's Facebook and Instagram businesses.

Meta's capital expenditure reached about $34.9 billion in the third quarter, exceeding the $32.8 billion generated from operating activities. Free cash flow turned negative at roughly $2.1 billion, underscoring the financial pressure of its AI infrastructure buildout.

Meta is placing its Muse AI agent at the centre of its future strategy. The product has attracted more than 10 million users in the US and Canada in its first six weeks, as the company seeks to turn its AI investments into a meaningful source of future revenue.

Meta's board approved a new class of publicly traded, non-voting Class C common stock. The structure is designed to give the company greater flexibility to fund investments, acquisitions and employee compensation while preserving Mark Zuckerberg's voting control.

Under the announced structure, eligible shareholders are expected to receive one non-voting Class C share for every existing Class A or Class B share. The distribution is expected to have the effect of a two-for-one split in the market price of Class A shares, without changing shareholders' voting power.

Meta expects fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, signalling continued momentum heading into the holiday advertising season. The outlook gives investors reason for optimism, although rising costs and legal expenses remain important risks to profitability.

Meta's earnings beat reinforces the strength of its advertising business, but heavy AI spending and negative free cash flow raise questions about returns on investment. Investors will watch whether new AI products generate enough revenue to justify the company's expanding capital commitments.
